([[Middletown, Rhode Island]]) | college = * [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] (2020–2021) * [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] (2021–2024) | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2024 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2024]]) * Second-team All-American – [[USBWA]], [[The Sporting News|SN]] ([[2023 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2023]]) * Third-team All-American – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] (2023) * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season assists leaders|NCAA season assists leader]] (2024) * [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] (2023) * 2× First-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2023, 2024) * [[Atlantic 10]] Rookie of the Year ([[2020–21 Atlantic 10 Conference men's basketball season|2021]]) * [[Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] MOP ([[2023 Big East men's basketball tournament|2023]]) }} '''Tyler Joseph Kolek''' (born March 27, 2001) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason Patriots]] and the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]]. ==Early life and high school career== Kolek grew up in [[Cumberland, Rhode Island]] and initially attended [[Cumberland High School (Rhode Island)|Cumberland High School]].{{cite web |last=Koch |first=Bill |date=January 29, 2022 |title=RI native Tyler Kolek playing for Marquette at The Dunk vs. PC |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/college/2022/01/29/rhode-island-native-tyler-kolek-marquette-university-providence-college-basketball/9267683002/ |access-date=March 7, 2023 |work=[[The Providence Journal]]}} He transferred to [[St. George's School (Rhode Island)|St. George's School]] prior to the start of his senior year. Kolek was named the Rhode Island Gatorade Boys Basketball Player of the Year as a junior after averaging 18.6 points, 8.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists, and 2.5 steals per game.{{cite web |last=Rueb |first=Eric |date=March 15, 2019 |title=St. George's junior Kolek named R.I. boys basketball Gatorade Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.newportri.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/15/st-georges-junior-kolek-named-ri-boys-basketball-gatorade-player-of-year/5698263007/ |access-date=March 7, 2023 |work=[[The Newport Daily News]]}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] over offers from [[Elon Phoenix men's basketball|Elon]], [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern]], [[Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball|Holy Cross]], and [[Vermont Catamounts men's basketball|Vermont]].{{cite web|url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/college/2019/09/17/st-georges-guard-cumberland-native-tyler-kolek-commits-to-george-mason/2765943007/|title=St. George's guard, Cumberland native Tyler Kolek commits to|first=Bill|last=Koch|work=[[The Providence Journal]]|date=September 17, 2019|access-date=March 7, 2023}} ==College career== Kolek began his college career at [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]].{{cite web |last=Kayata |first=Joe |date=January 14, 2021 |title=Homecoming for Cumberland's Kolek |url=https://turnto10.com/sports/content/homecoming-for-cumberlands-kolek |access-date=March 7, 2023 |website=[[turnto10.com]]}} He was named the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] Rookie of the Year as a freshman after averaging 10.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game.{{cite web |last=Koch |first=Bill |date=April 14, 2021 |title=George Mason transfer Tyler Kolek Marquette Shaka Smart |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/2021/04/14/george-mason-transfer-tyler-kolek-marquette-shaka-smart/7230318002/ |access-date=March 7, 2023 |work=[[The Providence Journal]]}} Following the end of the season, head coach [[Dave Paulsen]] was fired{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=March 16, 2021 |title=Paulsen out after six seasons at George Mason |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31076809 |access-date=March 27, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} and Kolek entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|url=https://turnto10.com/sports/content/cumberlands-kolek-to-enter-transfer-portal|title=Cumberland's Kolek enters transfer portal|first=Joe|last=Kayata|website=[[WJAR|TurnTo10.com]]|date=March 19, 2021|access-date=March 7, 2023}} Kolek ultimately transferred to [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].{{cite web |last=Steele |first=Ben |date=April 14, 2021 |title=Atlantic 10 freshman of year Tyler Kolek transfers to Marquette |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2021/04/14/atlantic-10-freshman-year-tyler-kolek-transfers-marquette/7230231002/ |access-date=March 7, 2023 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]}} He averaged 6.7 points per game and led the [[Big East Conference]] with 5.9 assists per game in his first season with the Golden Eagles.{{cite web|url=https://www.valleybreeze.com/sports/cumberlands-kolek-continues-to-excel-at-marquette-earns-big-east-player-of-week-honors/article_9990be54-a1dc-11ed-ade3-33284d8806d7.html|title=Cumberland's Kolek continues to excel at Marquette, earns Big East Player of Week honors|work=The Valley Breeze|date=February 2, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}} Kolek was named the [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] and first team All-Big East as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2023/03/05/marquettes-tyler-kolek-oso-ighodaro-kam-jones-earn-big-east-honors/69973679007/|title=Marquette's Tyler Kolek, Oso Ighodaro, Kam Jones earn Big East honors|first=Ben|last=Steele|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=March 5, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2023/03/08/marquettes-tyler-kolek-and-shaka-smart-big-east-top-player-and-coach/69983049007/|title=Big East honors Marquette's Tyler Kolek and Shaka Smart as conference's basketball player and coach of year|first=Ben|last=Steele|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=March 8, 2023|access-date=March 9, 2023}} He was also named the Most Outstanding Player of the [[2023 Big East men's basketball tournament|2023 Big East tournament]] after averaging 18.7 points, seven rebounds, and five assists in the three games.{{cite web |last=FLM |date=March 14, 2023 |title=Marquette aims to douse upset bid by 15-seed Vermont |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/marquette-aims-to-douse-upset-bid-by-15-seed-vermont/ |access-date=March 20, 2023 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}} Kolek averaged 12.9 points, 7.5 assists, 4.1 rebounds, and 1.8 steals over 36 games on the season.{{cite web|url=https://theathletic.com/5001990/2023/10/30/college-basketball-all-americans-zach-edey-tyler-kolek-hunter-dickinson/|title=Men’s college basketball preseason All-Americans: Edey, Kolek lead The Athletic’s list|first=Kyle|last=Tucker|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=December 8, 2023}} Kolek was named the preseason Big East Player of the Year as well as to multiple preseason All-American teams entering his senior season.{{cite web |date=October 24, 2023 |title=Marquette's Tyler Kolek is Big East preseason player of year |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2023/10/24/marquettes-tyler-kolek-is-big-east-preseason-player-of-year/71298607007/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=December 8, 2023
